contractCoverage.text: hermeticity: prove the suite makes no outbound HTTP even when OPENAI_API_KEY and EMBEDDING_BASE_URL are exported in the environment before vitest starts
evidence: Shell-level proof: ran the shipped, unmodified domain-proposal.test.ts with OPENAI_API_KEY and EMBEDDING_BASE_URL exported to a bogus API key and a closed local port (http://127.0.0.1:9) BEFORE invoking vitest. Suite completed in 468ms total (test bodies executed in 6ms), all non-skipped tests passed, no hang and no ECONNREFUSED-derived failure surfaced — consistent with the hash embedder being used throughout, never the openai/endpoint path.

Fetch-spy-level proof (stronger than timing alone): g001-red-team-gen4-hermeticity.test.ts reproduces the exact shipped idiom (hostile process.env values set first, then the same `vi.stubEnv('OPENAI_API_KEY','')` / `vi.stubEnv('EMBEDDING_BASE_URL','')` pair used in domain-proposal.test.ts:7-8) with `global.fetch` replaced by a spy that throws synchronously if ever called. describeEmbedder() reports 'hash' (not 'openai'/'embedding-endpoint'); resolveEmbedder()'s embedder resolves a vector in <50ms with zero fetch calls; a full generateDomainProposal() run (no deps.embed override, so it falls through to resolveEmbedder() exactly like the shipped semantic-hit case's internal call) also completes with zero fetch calls.

Negative control included to validate the fetch-spy is a real witness: the SAME hostile env WITHOUT the vi.stubEnv('') pin makes describeEmbedder() report something other than 'hash', and the fetch-spy DOES get called exactly once when the embedder is invoked (rejecting as expected against the closed port) — proving the spy would have caught a hermeticity violation had the pin been missing or broken.

contractCoverage.text: anti-tautology: confirm the new semantic-hit case would FAIL if the embedding term were removed — reasoning against hybridScore that tags:[] gives tagScore 0, so a null query embedding would drop the candidate entirely
evidence: g001-red-team-gen4-hermeticity.test.ts exercises the shipped hybridScore/recallHybrid/scoreDomainMemory functions directly (not the shipped test file) against the exact candidate/query shape from the new case (tags: [], embedding: [1,0,0], query.tags: []): with queryEmbedding=[1,0,0] (cosine sim 1), hybridScore returns 0.7 (default embeddingWeight, tagScore=0) and recallHybrid returns the record. With queryEmbedding=null, hybridScore falls into the !hasEmbedding branch (domain-embedding.ts:64-69) and returns exactly tagScore=0; recallHybrid's `.filter((entry) => entry.score > 0)` (domain-embedding.ts:97) then drops the record from the result set entirely — it is not merely ranked lower, it is absent.

Independently corroborated at the scoreDomainMemory level: scoreDomainMemory(query, record) === 0 for this exact pair, both because query.tags.length === 0 (domain-memory.ts:89, an explicit early-return) and because record.tags is also empty (zero overlap either way) — two independent reasons the tag path alone can never surface this candidate.

Conclusion: the shipped assertion `expect(seen.join('\n')).toContain('유사 딜 메모: 방화벽 갱신 할인 구조')` is load-bearing on the embedding term specifically — removing it would make the memory unrecallable and the assertion would fail, not merely weaken. Confirmed by direct library-function invocation rather than by editing the shipped test.

NON-BLOCKER (new, gen4 observation): the shipped domain-proposal.test.ts's env pin (`vi.stubEnv('OPENAI_API_KEY', '')` / `vi.stubEnv('EMBEDDING_BASE_URL', '')`) is scoped to that single test file (module-level `vi.stubEnv` calls apply for the lifetime of that test file's module instance, and vitest resets stubbed envs between files via its default isolation behavior). It does not protect OTHER test files in the same package from a hostile ambient environment unless they either carry the same pin themselves or never call resolveEmbedder()/generateDomainProposal() in the first place. Verified by grep this generation: domain-agent-runtime.test.ts and the gen1-3 __qa__ files (g001-red-team.test.ts, g001-red-team.integration.test.ts) each carry the identical stub pair; domain-polish.test.ts stubs EMBEDDING_BASE_URL per-test where it exercises resolveEmbedder(); project-decision.test.ts and project-decision.embedding.test.ts sidestep the issue entirely by importing the test-only `createHashEmbedder` from `./domain-embedder` and never calling the ambient `resolveEmbedder()` from `domain-embedder-openai.ts`, so no stub is needed there. This is a per-file discipline requirement, not a gap in the shipped fix; flagged only so a future new test file that DOES call resolveEmbedder()/generateDomainProposal() without copying this pin would silently regain live-HTTP risk on a machine with real keys set. Confirmed non-blocking for THIS delta since the shipped file is scoped correctly.
